title: Prompting and Retrieval
tagline: In-context learning, prompt design, structured output, embeddings, vector search and retrieval-augmented generation
summary: Much of what a language model can do is unlocked by what you put in its context. This course covers in-context learning and prompt design, structured output, text embeddings and vector search, retrieval-augmented generation and its evaluation, and the problem of hallucination.

overview: Prompting and retrieval augment LLMs at inference time. This course covers prompt engineering, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, and RAG.
The key insight is that prompts and retrieval can shape behavior without changing weights: the model adapts via context, not gradient updates.
outcomes: Describe prompt engineering: few-shot, CoT, self-consistency.
Explain RAG: embedding, retrieval, reranking, and augmentation.
Analyze prompt sensitivity and the fragility of few-shot learning.
Evaluate retrieval quality and answer faithfulness.

history.title: Chain of Thought
history.detail: Wei et al. showed chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in LLMs.

history.title: Self-consistency
history.detail: Wang et al. introduced self-consistency decoding over multiple reasoning paths.

history.title: RAG survey
history.detail: Lewis et al. surveyed retrieval-augmented generation methods.

chapters.title: In-context learning

chapters.title: Prompt design
chapters.summary: Instructions, examples, roles and formatting, and systematic prompt engineering.

chapters.title: Structured output
